section_1.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Area Operators
section_1.content: Briefly recall that a 2x2 determinant represents the signed area of a parallelogram formed by two column vectors. If the determinant is zero, the vectors are collinear (area collapses).
section_1.example: Visualizing two vectors, v1=(2,1) and v2=(1,2), forming a parallelogram in the Cartesian plane.

section_2.title: The Linear System as a Geometric Puzzle
section_2.content: Represent the system Ax = b as a vector equation: x1(column1) + x2(column2) = b. Explain that we are trying to find the 'weights' (x1, x2) that scale these columns to reach target vector b.
section_2.example: An archer (the vector b) stands at (5, 5). Two elastic bands (column vectors) must be stretched by factors x1 and x2 to hit the bullseye.

section_3.title: Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Insight)
section_3.content: Introduce Cramer’s Rule: x1 = det(A1)/det(A) and x2 = det(A2)/det(A). Explain that substituting the target vector b into the first column creates a new parallelogram whose area is scaled by x1.
section_3.example: Animation showing the original parallelogram defined by (col1, col2) being swapped for (b, col2) to reveal the area ratio.

section_4.title: Visual Proof: Area Scaling
section_4.content: Demonstrate that the ratio of the area of the 'substituted' parallelogram to the original parallelogram is exactly the value of the unknown variable. This provides the 'Aha!' moment.
section_4.example: A split-screen animation: Left side shows the variable x1 changing; right side shows the area of the modified parallelogram expanding and contracting in perfect synchronization.

section_5.title: Summary and Geometric Constraint
section_5.content: Conclude by noting that if det(A)=0, the column vectors are parallel (the area is zero), making division impossible—this is the geometric reason why systems with no unique solutions fail Cramer's Rule.
section_5.example: The 'Crushed Parallelogram': Two column vectors collapsing into a single line, rendering the target vector b unreachable unless it lies on that same line.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
